title: FSU's LEAP program welcomes third Tallahassee cohort and awards microgrants to alumni
text:
FSU’s LEAP program welcomes third Tallahassee cohort and awards microgrants to alumni
Florida State University's LEAP program began its third Tallahassee cohort with thirty-five local entrepreneurs this fall. Three alumni received surprise microgrants recognizing progress made since graduating from last year's program. Organizers say these efforts aim to support sustainable businesses among those facing adversity.
Florida State University’s Leon Entrepreneurship and Adversity Program welcomed 35 local entrepreneurs to its third Tallahassee cohort on Sept. 26, supporting participants as they build businesses while facing economic and other challenges. The event also recognized three graduates from the 2025 cohort with microgrants to support their business growth.
LEAP was launched in 2024 by FSU’s Jim Moran Institute for Global Entrepreneurship and the Jim Moran College of Entrepreneurship as part of the Urban Poverty and Business Initiative, a global network housed at the University of Notre Dame that uses entrepreneurship as a pathway out of poverty. The program returned for a second cohort in 2025. The ten-month initiative supports aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs in Leon, Gadsden, and Wakulla counties through a community bootcamp where they are mentored by local business owners and consulted by FSU students.
The current cohort is participating in a six-week community bootcamp running through Oct. 31, featuring twelve guest speakers including local entrepreneurs and community leaders. Susana Santos, Jim Moran Associate Professor of Entrepreneurship, said: “I am amazed by the powerful stories our participants bring with them and by the businesses they are building, many of them born from real needs they see in their own neighborhoods.”
Three LEAP 2025 alumni—Shishandra Devlin of Bougie With A Board, Sarah Babchuck of Love Story Book Co., and Latasha Davis of Wisdom Adult Day Care Services—returned to share their experiences on a panel before being surprised with microgrants for their businesses. The grants are awarded based on each entrepreneur’s progress through eighty steps toward creating a sustainable venture over ten months in LEAP. Two grants were supported by the Urban Poverty and Business Initiative network; one was funded by Bank of America.
Marina Lickson, Northwest Florida director at the Jim Moran Institute for Global Entrepreneurship, said: “These microgrants recognize the work our graduates keep putting in long after the bootcamp ends... A small grant at the right moment can make a big difference.” Devlin said: “LEAP has been an important part of my journey as an entrepreneur... Receiving this microgrant is an investment in Bougie With A Board’s continued growth...” Babchuck added: “The importance of the microgrant for our business cannot be understated as it will help us afford a new sign...” Davis said: “This microgrant will help us purchase engaging activity supplies... For me, this support is also a reminder that our work matters...”
Mike Brady, Interim Dean of the Jim Moran College, attended opening day ceremonies stating: “LEAP shows what is possible when a university invests in people around it... Seeing last year’s graduates return to celebrate their progress... is exactly the kind of impact we want to keep growing across Florida.” In August 2026, another similar program launched at FSU's West Palm Beach Collaboration Space.
